notes: The petition is fiction by the owner. CREATOR is intentionally the requester's wallet, 0x70c6C4fcaAb11151FCEDb32eaaC3431547193A0a, and receives exactly 1.64 ETH only in the transaction that retires medallion #447 to DEAD. There is no admin or beneficiary setter. FareToken has a zero-argument constructor. Hook permissions are 0x10CC, validated by the constructor; the deployed address must satisfy (uint160(address) & 0x3fff) == 0x10CC. The hook requires a Cancun-compatible EVM for its transient reentrancy lock on slot 1. Deploy with the chain's PoolManager as the sole argument and atomically initialize the intended native-ETH/FARE447 pool, because the first native-ETH pool permanently becomes launchPool and only that pool accrues fees. Initial price is the decimal sqrtPriceX96 79228162514264337593543950336 (2**96), assuming one FARE447 per ETH; both currencies have 18 decimals. MEDALLION_NFT, IMD and POOL4 addresses are fixed mainnet constants: retire(), burnIMD() and pokeAnchor() require mainnet and revert on every other chain, including Sepolia. The NFT's current owner must approve the hook unless the NFT is already at DEAD. Fees accrue as PoolManager claims; swap callbacks make no ETH payment or IMD purchase. Permissionless retire() verifies the NFT is at DEAD and pays CREATOR atomically; a failure rolls back the transaction. Fees above the reserved cap are available to permissionless burnIMD() calls even before retirement. IMD purchases use bounded batches, fixed pools and reference-price guards in separate top-level calls. All purchased IMD goes to the fixed DEAD sink, 0x000000000000000000000000000000000000dEaD; this does not invoke IMD's supply-reduction function. Callers receive no reward. Donations do not enter the ledger. See README.md and docs/operations.md for accounting, fallback behavior and keeper responsibilities.
